heading: INTRODUCTION
src: I propose to write how I became a Christian and not ivhy, The so-called “philosophy of conversion ” is not my theme. I will only describe its tL phenomena,” and will furnish materials for more disciplined minds than mine to philosophize upon. I^early contracted the habit of keeping my diary, in which I noted down whatever ideas and events that came to pass upon me. I made myself a subject of careful observations, and found it more: mysterious than anything I ever have studied. I jotted’ down its rise and progress, its falls and backslidings, its joys and hopes, its sins and darkness; and notwithstanding all the awfulness that attends such an observation like this, I found it more seriously interesting than any study I ever have undertaken. I call my diary a w log-book,” as a book in which is entered the daily progress of this poor bark toward the upper haven through sins, and tears, and many a woe. I might just as well call it a “biologist’s sketch-book,” in which is kept the accounts of all the morphological and physiological changes of a soul in its embryological development from a seed to a full-eared com. A part of such a record is now given to the public, and the reader may draw whatever conclusions he likes from it. My diary, however begins only few months before I accepted Christianity.
zh: 我打算記述我如何成為基督徒，而非為何成為基督徒。所謂「回心的哲學」並非我的題旨。我只欲描繪其「現象」，並為比我更具理性思辨能力的人們提供進一步哲學思考的材料。我自幼養成了記日記的習慣，將降臨於我身上的一切思想與事件一一記錄其下。我把自己當作仔細觀察的對象，發現它比我所研究過的任何事物都更為神秘。我記下了它的興起與進展、其衰落與退步、其喜樂與希望、其罪惡與黑暗；儘管進行如此觀察所伴隨的種種可怖之處，我卻發現它比我所從事過的任何研究都更加嚴肅而有趣。我稱我的日記為「航海日誌」，乃是一部記載這艘卑微之舟每日朝著上界港灣航進的紀錄——透過罪惡、淚水與無數的苦難而行。我不妨也稱之為「生物學家的速寫本」，其中記載了一個靈魂在其胚胎發育過程中的種種形態學與生理學變化——從一粒種籽發展至充實飽滿的穀穗。這樣一份紀錄的片段如今呈現於世人面前，讀者可據之得出他所欲得出的任何結論。然而，我的日記實則僅始於我接納基督教前數月之事。
